top_choice_rationale: Base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) is a new chemical act on DNA, deamination at a programmed site without cleavage, so it is distinct from the 2020 guided-cleavage prize. The adenine editor needed a TadA evolved to act on DNA, outcomes are measurable at nucleotide resolution and reproduced widely, and clinical use has begun. The trio follows the actual sequence of the work, although the Kondo/Nishida Target-AID priority question and the short clinical record are real reservations. Degraders (P004) are second on maturity but join two lineages; C-N coupling (P003) is mature and cleanly attributed but overlaps the 2010 prize; lipid nanoparticles (P002) have an attribution problem; no award ranks last because several candidacies are prize-worthy.
